Spec review companion · #7 · snapshot 4b59459 · 2026-11-14

A saved limits reading past its reset time is never deleted

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #7

The change

A session can start with a saved limits reading whose limits are all past their reset time. The band shows no limits, which is correct, but the record stays in the mod's storage with no end. assessment.md:35

The fix: the session.start hook now deletes the saved reading when it has no limit left in its window. The band shows the same as before. fix.md:10

1mod file changed fix.md:18
12hooks tests added or updated fix.md:33 fix.md:66 fix.md:74
6checks passed, 0 failed test.md:15
1check not run: the band in a real session test.md:25
4deviations from the assessment fix.md:59

Root cause

The start of a session filters the saved reading for the view, but no code compares the result with what is stored. follow deletes only when the view had limits before. A view that never had limits never meets this. assessment.md:58

Remediation chosen

Delete in the session.start hook when a record is stored and withSaved(EMPTY, saved, now).limits is empty. It is the same rule that decides what the band shows. view.ts does not change. assessment.md:66

The delete comes last

It runs after the view, the agents count and the timer. A delete that fails costs the session nothing, and the next start tries again. assessment.md:76

Patch release 0.1.1

The change is in the mod, so the version goes up, with a CHANGELOG.md entry. fix.md:23

How it works

Examples

These are the hooks tests. They ran in the test kit, not in a real session.

All limits past their reset

One five_hour limit, reset one minute ago. The band shows nothing, and the record is gone. This is the reported case. fix.md:37

One limit past, one ahead

The band shows the limit that is ahead. The record stays as it was: the mod does not rewrite it. fix.md:40

Reset time equal to now

It counts as passed, as in the band's own rule. fix.md:39

The session has its own limits

The old record is still deleted, and the band shows the session's own limits. The check does not depend on the view. fix.md:45

The delete fails

The session still has its band and its timer, and the start event still ends. fix.md:47

What breaks for someone else

WhoWhat changesWhere listed
A user of the bandNothing. The view is built as before.assessment.md:114
A user on an account with no limitsAn old saved reading leaves storage at the next start.assessment.md:115
A user on an account with limitsAn old record is deleted at the start, and the first answer saves a new one. Nothing is lost.assessment.md:117

What to check before approving

  1. The hooks tests no longer use mock.store. The store in the tests is a Map of the test's own. A difference in how the real store answers a delete would not show. fix.md:63 test.md:45
  2. docs/architecture.md changed, and the assessment did not list it. Its diagram shows each call to the store at the start. fix.md:61
  3. The band was not read in a real session. The release run after the merge does that. test.md:25
  4. No try around the delete. The plan relies on Claude Code to skip a hook whose call fails. Check that this is still the rule you want. assessment.md:76
  5. Principle I. The change deletes the mod's own record and keeps nothing new. assessment.md:128
  6. Principle V. Each failure path in the plan has a hooks test. Compare the two lists. assessment.md:132 fix.md:33
  7. A small gap stays between the second read and the delete. The store has no call that checks and deletes in one step. A reading saved in that gap is lost until that session's next answer. fix.md:66 test.md:47

The notes defer nothing on purpose: there is no open question and no follow-up. assessment.md:120

Look-ups

Glossary
  • Saved reading: the latest limits reading, kept in $.store under the key limits, so that a new session can show limits before its own first answer.
  • In its window: a limit whose reset time is still ahead.
  • follow: the function in runway.ts that updates the view and keeps the saved reading in step.

# Bug Assessment: A saved limits reading past its reset time is never deleted - **Slug**: 007-delete-expired-limits-reading- **Created**: 2026-11-14- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #7 of `tmathura/claude-runway`)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: low ## Report (verbatim or summarized) > A saved limits reading whose reset time has passed can stay in the mod's storage with no end.>> - At the start of a session, `withSaved` (`plugins/runway/hooks/lib/view.ts:149`) leaves out each>   saved limit whose reset time has passed. The view then has no limits.> - `follow` (`plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts:122`) deletes the saved reading only when the view had>   limits before the update (line 128). The view had none, so nothing is deleted.> - On an account that has no usage limits, no new reading replaces the old one. The record stays>   under the key `limits` in `$.store`.>> The record holds a window name, a share used and a reset time only. It is never shown, because its> reset time has passed. `docs/configuration.md` ("What the mod keeps") says that such a reading can> stay. CodeRabbit found this in the review of PR #6. The issue asks for this: - Delete the saved reading at the start of a session when no saved limit is still in its window.- Keep a saved reading that has one or more limits still in their window.- Do not change what the band shows.- Do not add a network request, a file read or a file write.- Update the row for the saved reading in `docs/configuration.md`.- The change is a patch release, with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry. ## Symptom A session starts with a saved reading in `$.store` (key `limits`) whose limits are all past theirreset time. The band shows no limits, which is correct, but the record stays in storage. It must bedeleted, so that storage holds only a reading that can still be shown. ## Reproduction 1. Put a reading in the store under `limits`, with one limit whose `resetsAt` is in the past.2. Start a session on an account that reports no limits (`rateLimits: []`).3. Read `$.store.get("limits")`. It still returns the old record. Later turns do not delete it. The code shows this without a run: see "Root Cause Hypothesis". ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts:25-29` — the `session.start` hook reads the saved reading and  the time, and passes them to `withSaved`. It never writes to the store.- `plugins/runway/hooks/lib/view.ts:149-159` — `withSaved` leaves out each saved limit whose reset  time is not ahead of `now`. It is pure, so it cannot delete the record.- `plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts:122-131` — `follow` deletes the saved reading only when the view  had limits before the update (`had`). A view that started with no limits never meets this. ## Root Cause Hypothesis The start of a session filters the saved reading for the view, but no code compares the resultwith what is stored. `follow` is the only place that deletes, and it deletes only on a change from"limits" to "no limits" in the view. A view that never had limits makes no such change. So arecord with no limit left in its window stays until a new reading replaces it, and on an accountwith no limits that never happens. Confidence: high. ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: In the `session.start` hook of `plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts`, as its last stepbefore `return next(e)`, delete the saved reading when a record is stored (`saved !== undefined`)and `withSaved(EMPTY, saved, now).limits` is empty. This uses the saved reading and the time that thehook has already read, and the same rule that decides what the band shows, so the two cannotdisagree. `EMPTY` is used, not the session's view, so the answer depends only on the record: a viewthat already has limits makes `withSaved` return early. `view.ts` does not change. A stored value that is not a reading (not an object, or with no usable limit) gives an empty listtoo, so it is deleted. It can never be shown. The delete is the last step, after the view, the agents count and the timer, so a delete thatfails costs the session nothing. The hook has no `try` around the call: Claude Code skips a hookwhose call on `$` fails, runs the rest of the chain and names the mod in the debug log(`specs/001-session-runway-band/research.md`, §7). The record then stays, and the next start triesagain. **Alternatives**: - Send the start through `follow`. Rejected: `had` is false for a view with no limits, so the  record would still stay, and a valid saved reading would be written back at each start.- A new pure function in `view.ts` that says whether a saved reading holds. Rejected: it repeats  what `withSaved(EMPTY, ...)` already gives. **Files likely to change**: - `plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts`- `plugins/runway/tests/runway.test.ts`- `docs/configuration.md`- `plugins/runway/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (patch release 0.1.1) **Tests to add or update** (hooks tests, with the mock clock and the mock store): - A session that starts with a saved reading whose limits are all past their reset time: the band  shows nothing, and `limits` is gone from the store.- A session that starts with a saved reading that has one limit past its reset time and one still  in its window: the band shows the limit in its window, and the record stays as it was.- A reset time equal to `now` counts as passed.- A start with nothing stored deletes nothing and does not fail.- A stored value of the wrong form (not an object, or a limit with no reset time) is deleted, and  the band shows nothing.- A saved reading with a window name the mod does not know and a share of zero, whose reset time  is ahead, stays in the store.- A delete that fails: the session still has its band and its timer, and the event still ends.- A session whose own first reading has limits, with a saved reading past its reset time: the  record is deleted, and the band shows the session's own limits. ## Risks & Considerations - The band does not change: the view is built as before, and the delete comes after it.- The delete is one more call to `$.store` at the start, only when a record with no limit left is  stored. It adds no network request and no file access by the mod itself.- A session on an account with limits that starts with an old record deletes it, and its first  answer saves a new one through `follow`. Nothing is lost: the old record could not be shown. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check | Principle | State | Proof || --- | --- | --- || I. Watch only | met | The hook still returns `next(e)` unchanged. The change only deletes the mod's own record of numbers, times and window names. It keeps nothing new. || II. A missing reading never breaks the band | met | Nothing stored, or a stored value of the wrong form, does not throw: `withSaved` already handles both. Hooks tests cover a start with nothing stored. `claude plugin validate` must pass. || III. Small, own code, no dependencies | met | A few lines in one hook. No dependency, no new part, option or layer. || IV. Every surface, every system | not relevant | The band's tree and its width rule do not change. || V. Tested, including failure paths | met | Hooks tests for a reset time in the past, a reset time equal to now, a mixed reading, no reading, a stored value of the wrong form, an unknown window name with a share of zero, and a delete that fails. The release run follows the merge. || Versioning | met | Patch release 0.1.1 with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry; `npm run check-version` must pass. |

# Bug Fix: A saved limits reading past its reset time is never deleted - **Slug**: 007-delete-expired-limits-reading- **Fixed**: 2026-11-14- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary The `session.start` hook now deletes the saved limits reading when it has no limit left in itswindow. The check uses `withSaved(EMPTY, saved, now)`, the same rule that decides what the bandshows. The band shows the same as before. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/runway/hooks/runway.ts` | modified | The delete is the last step of the `session.start` hook, before `return next(e)` || `plugins/runway/tests/runway.test.ts` | modified, tests added | The store is now a `Map` of the test's own, so a test can read what the mod left in it || `docs/configuration.md` | modified | The row for the saved reading in "What the mod keeps" || `docs/architecture.md` | modified | One line in the diagram "From an event to the view" || `plugins/runway/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | The entry for 0.1.1 || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/runway/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | Version 0.1.1, set by `npm run bump-version -- 0.1.1` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```tsif (saved !== undefined && withSaved(EMPTY, saved, now).limits.length === 0) {  await $.store.delete(SAVED_LIMITS);}``` ## Tests Added or Updated All in `plugins/runway/tests/runway.test.ts`: - `a saved reading whose reset time has passed is not shown, and is deleted` — the record is gone  from the store (updated: it checked only the band before).- `a saved reading whose reset time is now counts as passed` — a reset time equal to now.- `a saved reading with one limit still in its window stays, and that limit shows` — the record  stays as it was.- `a saved reading of a window the mod does not know, with nothing used, stays while its reset is ahead`.- `a stored value that is not a reading is deleted` — and another key in the store stays.- `a saved limit with no reset time is deleted`.- `a session with its own limits deletes a saved reading whose reset time has passed` — the band  shows the session's own limits.- `a delete that fails leaves the band and the timer, and the start still ends`.- `with no reading the mod draws nothing of its own` — also checks that nothing is written when  nothing is stored (updated). ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev` → ok; `npm run build` → no errors; `npm test` → 242 passed,  0 failed, 10 skipped; `npm run check-version` → all match 0.1.1;  `claude plugin validate plugins/runway` → Validation passed;  `claude plugin test plugins/runway` → 23 passed, 0 failed.- Manual checks: none. The band was not read in a real session; the release run does that. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-11-14: `docs/architecture.md` also changed. The assessment did not list it. Its diagram  shows each call to the store at the start of a session, so it needed the new delete.- 2026-11-14: the hooks tests no longer use `mock.store`. The test kit gives no way to read that  store, and it allows one hook for each event, so a second hook cannot watch the calls. The tests  answer `store.get`, `store.set` and `store.delete` from a `Map` instead.- 2026-11-14 (review round 1): the hook reads the store again just before the delete, and deletes  only when that reading also has no limit left in its window. The assessment used the reading  from the start of the hook alone. Another session can save a new reading between that read and  the delete, and the delete would have removed it. The store has no call that checks and deletes  in one step, so a save between the second read and the delete can still be lost; that session's  next answer saves it again. New test: `a reading that another session saves during the start is  not deleted`. The test for a start with nothing stored now also counts the delete calls. The  hooks tests then gave 24 passed, 0 failed.- 2026-11-14 (review round 2): tests and docs only; the hook did not change. The test for a  reading saved during the start now changes the store at the hook's second read, so it no longer  depends on the order of the calls in the hook. Two new tests cover the other answers of the  second read: the record is gone (no delete is sent), and another reading with no limit left  (it is deleted). The diagram in `docs/architecture.md` now shows the second read. The hooks  tests then gave 26 passed, 0 failed. ## Follow-ups None.
